title: Machine identity check
text: This note describes a fictional gateway used by a small reporting service. Its procedures belong to the pilot scenario, not to a deployed product. The examples concern machine identities rather than interactive employee sessions. The gateway authenticates a service account by validating a signed challenge with the public key registered for that account. A fresh nonce prevents replay. Failed signatures stop the request before any resource policy is read. Operators inspect the challenge result and account identifier in the audit record. Passing this check establishes the caller's identity; it does not by itself assign any permission or grant access to reports.

title: Independent packet checks

title: Contractor read denial
text: The release repository is a fictional collection of build artifacts. Its contractor group is separate from employee and automation groups. Changes below apply only to this repository and are evaluated using its small local permission table. Set the contractor group's read entry to deny and save the repository ACL. This explicit denial takes precedence over a broader read grant inherited from another local group. Verify the result using a contractor read request while leaving employee permissions unchanged. Existing artifacts remain stored in the repository. Denying reads does not delete artifacts or prevent a separately authorized publisher from uploading a new build.

title: Branch log rotation
text: A fictional branch lab has a firewall with separate inspection modes and a monitoring panel. The lab routes traffic through only the configured mode during a test. The descriptions below explain local behavior rather than vendor configuration syntax. Decision logs rotate when a local file reaches the configured storage limit. The newest file receives subsequent events while older files remain readable until the retention task removes them. Rotation affects log storage, not packet treatment or the selected inspection mode. If a diagnostic interval spans a rotation, read both adjacent files and order events by timestamp rather than by filename alone.

title: Printable archive transport
text: The transfer service in this scenario moves prepared archives between two isolated work areas. Operators have separate preparation and receiving accounts. Names of buttons and files below are invented for this dataset and are not instructions for a real service. The text transport option applies base64 encoding to an archive container so it can pass through a channel that accepts printable characters. Decoding reconstructs the same container bytes. This operation uses no secret key and does not provide confidentiality. It neither encrypts a plaintext archive nor decrypts a sealed one, even though the display becomes unreadable to someone expecting ordinary file contents.
